The user is now considering the red monopoly as a defensive buffer. Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois each have one house, though only Illinois has a house while the others are empty. The rent for that single house on Illinois is $100.

The $140 offer does not cover the green properties. Two houses on Pacific or NC cost $390, and three houses on Pennsylvania cost $1,000. Even one house on the red set would only yield $90 in rent. Virginia with three houses costs $500, which is still lethal. The cash buffer would only survive lighter pink and brown rents.

That would create a $250–$300 rent strip on the most frequently landed properties.

They calculate that p3 needs at least $210 after the trade to unmortgage New York and build three houses evenly, which would leave them with roughly $100. To prevent any immediate building, they should demand at least $298. They are now weighing whether to ask for $400 instead.

They are also checking whether St. Charles, which belongs to p2, would be a fatal landing.
